role: read-only AI researcher; no human review claimed
viability: A focused article on scribal institutions and community memory is supported. A definitive formation date, founder, comprehensive regional branches or current community survey is not supported. Avoid pretending this is a complete genealogy.

sources.title: Odisha District Gazetteers: Bhadrak
claims: The district account describes Karanas as scribes who wrote charters and documents and served government and zamindars as clerks, accountants and petty officials.
It associates grants of unassessed land as remuneration with some becoming landlords. Attribute this historical explanation to the gazetteer; no individual charter or dated grant is supplied here.

The preceding writing-history paragraph describes palm leaves and iron pens, zamindari land records, and a later shift towards quill, locally prepared ink and paper during British rule. That paragraph describes regional writing practice, not an exclusively Karana practice.
limits: Compiled2015–16 context; exact publication imprint not resolved here.
The text reproduces hierarchical caste classifications and essentialist praise. Do not adopt either.
Its phrase originally scribes is a summary, not documentary proof of a single caste-creation event.

sources.title: Rajata Kanta Dash, Vernacular Histories and History 2: Configuring Madalapanji of Odisha
sources.status: actual author-uploaded full article text inspected; official issue fetch timed out
sources.locator: printed p63, Madalapanji section; p64 continuation and bibliography
claims: Dash connects Karana record keepers with the Puri temple chronicle. He explicitly says its actual starting date is unknown before describing the traditional attribution to Chodaganga.

His account presents twenty-four Karana families as tradition, with five entrusted with writing and preserving the Madalapanji through Panjia, Tadau, Deula, Kotha and Baithi duties. This temple-service foundation narrative does not establish the creation of the entire community.

The records concern more than royal succession: inventories, ceremonial routines and royal orders; the Desa Khanja section concerns temple land grants and property. He also notes variant versions and embellishment by legend.
limits: RG upload date November2024 is not the article publication date.
Author is synthesizing earlier editions; underlying manuscripts and R.P.Chanda1927 were not independently inspected.
Do not adopt his unqualified later assertion of twelfth-century text dating after he acknowledges uncertain beginnings.

sources.title: CIIL Bhasha Sanchika catalog: ମାଦଳାପାଞ୍ଜି
sources.status: full institutional catalog metadata inspected; book PDF not inspected
claims: Catalog records an Odia PDF/book, issued2020, edited by Artaballabh Mohanti, published by Odisha Sahitya Akademi, extent74; not a documentary film.

Its abstract describes palm-leaf temple records concerning ceremonial practice and rulers; it attributes keeping them across generations to three Karana families and labels the Chodaganga start as supposed.
limits: Catalog abstract only; neither proof of three current families nor a count of the whole community.
Different numbers from Dash should not be merged or reconciled without manuscript/service research.
Best used only to show continuing publication and institutional preservation, not as independent proof of medieval origins.

rejected_leads: Utkal Historical Research Journal2023 caste-synthesis pages89–90 makes medieval epigraphy and equivalence claims without original inscriptions inspected; omit formation dates and Kayastha equivalence.
Bhattacharya1896 p189 explicitly distinguishes Orissa Karans from NorthBihar Karans, but outsider categorical taxonomy does not prove modern relationships; unnecessary to public narrative.
narrative_plan: Central question: what did keeping records mean in Odisha's institutions, and what can that tell us about Karana history without inventing a founder?
Start with concrete charters, land accounts and temple routines; explain a durable association with scribal work, not an inherited intellectual trait.
Use Bhadrak district history to connect service, remuneration and possible landholding; mark this as regional historical account.
Use Puri chronicle and differentiated duties to show preservation as skilled institutional work. Separate Chodaganga tradition from verified chronology explicitly.
Optional brief1825 witness demonstrates that the occupational association was documented, while withholding unsupported alias equations.
Close with manuscript preservation and the open question of family histories, training and changing careers; do not invent uniform wedding practices or claim all members still write records.
media: No verified licensed community-specific image. Text-first is appropriate. Neither general palm-leaf image nor surname implies maker's caste; any manuscript image requires independent rights verification.
